Clock speed is becoming increasingly more irrelevant as a measure of processing power. It is kept around as a marketing tool. How many operations a chip can perform in a second is far more important, and that number is not represented by clock speed.

The most compelling thing about this is that a single path can be encoded with multiple different information streams along different spectrum. This has the advantage of increased bandwidth along a single path. However, the streams still need to be interpreted, which means electrical parts. While light in a fiber optic tube travels at the speed of light, electricity only travels at the speed of light in a vacuum. Electrical parts will continue to be a bottleneck for speed.
